A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable and matchable text, figures, tables, equations, and references. Neither contains an appendix. The shorter length of v3 results from front-matter reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original descriptive analysis of its surveyed literature: quarterly publication counts in Figure 1 and deduplicated subdomain citation counts in Figure 3, whose center reports 282 papers. These qualify as data-analysis results, although the model-performance findings are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3 retains the survey's original literature-count analysis in the unnumbered cover plot and Figure 2, including the 282-paper coverage total. Retained original data-analysis results qualify even without new model experiments.

M1.justification: The surveyed algorithms and model components are unchanged. Neither version introduces a new code-generation algorithm, and the abstract's shortened descriptions do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The literature corpus, four-domain coverage, and benchmark inventory are unchanged. No training or evaluation dataset, task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same cited systems and comparison methods are discussed throughout. Neither version reports an original model-versus-baseline evaluation, and no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: The January 2026 literature snapshot, screening and coding rules, and manual verification procedure remain unchanged. Reported benchmark sample sizes, metrics, and evaluation settings also match.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or empirical case study is added or removed. The task illustrations and discussions of existing studies' failure modes are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same descriptive literature counts without uncertainty intervals or significance testing. No repeated-run information, seed reporting, or statistical estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: The quarterly publication counts, 282-paper coverage graphic, and benchmark-table entries match. Section 3.1 retains the cited IWR-Bench findings of 64.25% visual fidelity and 24.39% interactive function; no numerical or qualitative result changes.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same task definitions and Equations 1–7. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The shorter abstract omits some examples and descriptive categories, but the four-domain scope, code-role organization, and four verification-centered research directions remain intact. The introduction and conclusion retain the same substantive contributions.

C2.justification: The domain interpretations, future directions, and Section 8 limitations are unchanged. Sentence-level edits in Section 3.1.2 preserve the existing distinctions between visual appearance and functional correctness.

D1.justification: Survey methodology and technical disclosures remain unchanged. The abstract replaces the displayed repository URL with linked text reading 'GitHub', but the hyperlink target is identical, preserving resource access.

R1.justification: The reference list and cited-work membership are unchanged. The survey retains its positioning relative to text-based code generation and existing multimodal methods.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed by shortening examples, code-role descriptions, and the resource statement. Two passages in Section 3.1.2 receive sentence-level edits; the substantive section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract now fits on the first page, and the contents occupy one page with bold section entries instead of spilling the conclusion entry onto another page. The retained cover plot loses its caption and number, subsequent figures are renumbered, and the methodology contains an incomplete 'Figures 2 and' reference. Other figure and table displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The condensed abstract and consolidated contents improve concision and front-matter layout, but the missing publication-trend caption and incomplete figure reference reduce presentation clarity. These limited gains and defects leave overall quality essentially unchanged: the survey's coverage, evidence, mathematical formulations, synthesis, and limitations are retained.
